ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Martin Luther Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient visit for attacks of vertigo with left-ear tinnitus and muffled hearing, and low mood: history, neurological and ear examination, blood and urine tests, depression and safety screening, and an otology referral. Concerns: He is frightened of another attack, especially while preaching or teaching, and of losing the hearing in his left ear; He has felt low and abandoned for weeks and wonders whether the attacks are a spiritual trial rather than an illness; He remembers the pain of the stone last year and wants to avoid another. [S]

tr.td: Meclizine 25 mg tablet, one by mouth up to every 8 hours during a severe vertigo attack only, for no more than 3 days at a time
every 8 hours as needed during a severe attack, at most 3 days at a time
Naproxen 500 mg tablet, one by mouth twice daily with food for up to 7 days for stone pain
twice daily with food for up to 7 days
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg capsule, one by mouth daily for up to 4 weeks or until the stone passes
once daily until the stone passes
Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg tablet, one by mouth each morning
Sertraline 25 mg tablet, one by mouth each morning for one week
Sertraline 50 mg tablet, one by mouth each morning

Advance care planning conversation, about 16 minutes
Pure-tone and speech audiometry with tympanometry

text.paragraph: Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

tr.td: Recurrent spiritual crises with anxiety, fear and a deeply troubled conscience since his years as a monk in his twenties, which he called Anfechtungen
Headaches with noises in the ears since his late twenties, and headaches with faint spells and dizziness reported by his physician for about four years
Painful constipation with sleeplessness in his late thirties
A urinary stone passed last year after excruciating pain, preceded by headache, heaviness in the head, dizziness and nausea
Severe low mood earlier this year during bitter disputes in his work

list.item: Recurrent attacks of spinning vertigo for about three months, the worst twelve days ago, lasting hours, with roaring tinnitus, fullness and muffled hearing in the left ear and nausea, the tinnitus persisting between attacks; with low mood, poor sleep and loss of interest; cause not established at intake: an inner-ear disorder suspected, with vestibular migraine, vestibular schwannoma and posterior circulation stroke to be excluded and depression to be assessed; otology consultation requested: resolved, confirmed [S]

Ménière disease of the left ear, definite (AAO-HNS 2020 and Bárány Society criteria), with low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and persistent tinnitus in the left ear; vestibular migraine considered and judged unlikely as the main cause; vestibular schwannoma excluded by MRI: active, confirmed [S]

Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate (DSM-5-TR), with low mood, poor sleep, loss of interest, guilt and fatigue for about two months, after earlier periods of spiritual crisis and low mood; no suicidal ideation: active, confirmed [S]
Urinary stone disease: one stone passed spontaneously last year after severe pain; stone type and metabolic risk not yet known at intake: active, confirmed [S]

Right distal ureteral stone, 5 mm, at the ureterovesical junction, with mild right hydronephrosis and renal colic; no infection; kidney function normal; managed with naproxen and tamsulosin; passed nine days later; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for attacks of vertigo with left-ear tinnitus and muffled hearing, and low mood: history, neurological and ear examination, blood and urine tests, depression and safety screening, and an otology referral
Two-week review and otology consultation with audiometry; diagnoses of Ménière disease and recurrent depression
Six-week review: attacks, MRI result, thiazide and sertraline safety, mood, and the passed stone
Thirteen-week review: attacks, repeat audiogram, mood, and the 24-hour urine for stone prevention
Same-day sick visit for right flank pain

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Otology (neurotology) consultation in two weeks, with audiometry, to confirm the cause of the attacks and plan treatment

Diagnostic work-up at intake: ear and neurological examination, positional testing, blood count, kidney function and electrolytes, calcium, uric acid, TSH and urinalysis; a symptom diary of each attack (start, duration, hearing, tinnitus, ear fullness, headache, light sensitivity); formal audiometry at the otology visit
Meclizine only for severe attacks, for no more than three days at a time; sit or lie down at the first warning; no driving, ladders or swimming alone while attacks are active
Depression: PHQ-9 at every visit, a structured diagnostic interview at the next visit, and a safety plan with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number
Stone history: drink enough water to pass at least 2.5 liters of urine a day; serum calcium and uric acid at intake; stone analysis and metabolic testing if another stone occurs

Ménière disease: education; sodium 1,500 to 2,300 mg a day; caffeine and alcohol limited; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily as maintenance, with sodium and potassium checked at the next visit; no betahistine; MRI of the internal auditory canals with gadolinium; repeat audiogram at about three months; intratympanic steroid held in reserve if disabling attacks continue after three months

Recurrent depression: weekly cognitive behavioral therapy with behavioral activation, and sertraline 25 mg daily for a week, then 50 mg, by shared decision; sodium checked on sertraline with the thiazide
Right ureteral stone: naproxen for pain, tamsulosin as medical expulsive therapy for up to four weeks, urine strained and the stone sent for analysis, and renal ultrasound after passage
Vestibular rehabilitation for unsteadiness between attacks: a home program taught by a vestibular physical therapist

Stone prevention from the 24-hour urine: fluids to at least 2.5 liters of urine a day, sodium restriction with a dietitian, normal dietary calcium, citrus fruit for citrate, thiazide continued, and a repeat 24-hour urine in about six months
Fewer and milder vertigo attacks: no more than one disabling attack a month by three months, and able to preach without fear of an attack
One attack between the second and six-week visits and none in the five weeks before the thirteen-week visit; preaching again
Depression response (PHQ-9 down by at least 50 percent) by three months
PHQ-9 6 at thirteen weeks, down 60 percent from 15
Sodium intake below 2,300 mg a day
24-hour urine sodium 140 mmol (about 3,200 mg) at thirteen weeks: improved but above target
Urine volume of at least 2.5 liters a day
24-hour urine volume 1.6 liters at thirteen weeks

list.item: Independent; had to stop preaching mid-sermon during one attack and was unable to work for about a week after the worst one; fears an attack in public [S]

Well-built man, articulate and forceful; mood low, affect constricted but reactive, warming when he speaks of his work; describes guilt and a sense of being abandoned during the attacks; no suicidal ideation, intent or plan; no psychotic features; insight good [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 2026-07-28: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. No suicidal ideation, intent, plan or past attempts; during the worst attack he believed he would die but did not wish to. Outpatient care with a safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number, and review at every visit [S]
